text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: kv_cache_cardinality spike on cluster rope-ntk-canary (sliding-window prefetch). p95 gen latency up 3.2x, 5xx rate ~6%. Trigger: kv_cardinality > 200k. Auto-page: SRE on-call.

jordan-oncall: I'm on it — thanks bot. Who rolled the sliding-window prefetch to canary this morning?

priya-sre: looks like runaway kv entries. metric shard: kv_entries jumped from ~18k -> ~1.1M in ~7m on canary nodes. continuous-batcher backlog also spiking.

matt-runtime: that was my canary rollout (08:12 deploy). Config on canary: PREFETCH_WINDOW=4096, PREFETCH_STRIDE=128, ENABLE_YARN=true. Confirming huge unique kv prefixes on those instances.

sam-rl: this matches an NTK/YaRN interaction we feared — longer effective prefixes from NTK expansions combined with sliding-window prefetch produce many distinct cache keys per request. Batching those requests without dedupe gives near combinatorial growth.

emily-support: customer impact check — do we have affected tenants? any SLO breaches visible?

priya-sre: quick customer scan: two Dedicated tenants (acme-co, bizly) show elevated 5xx for generation endpoints. Hosted API error spike lasted ~3m and mostly recovered with retries. No data-plane leaks.

devon-eng: can we toggle the feature or revert the canary quickly?

jordan-oncall: mitigation plan (initial):
1) pause sliding-window prefetch on canary (feature-flag)
2) throttle continuous-batcher (max_batch_size=8, max_wait_ms=20)
3) enable temporary kv-cardinality cap + run compaction
Assign: matt -> pause flag, devon -> throttle, priya -> compaction / monitoring.

matt-runtime: pausing sliding-window via admin API now.

matt-runtime: command I used:
```
curl -X POST "https://admin.redwood.internal/flags/rope/sliding_window" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"enabled":false}'
```

matt-runtime: flag set, canary pods picked up config within 30s. PREFETCH_WINDOW shows 0 in /config on canary.

devon-eng: applying batch throttle to canary runtime env now.
```
kubectl -n inference set env deploy/rope-runtime-cont-canary CONTINUOUS_BATCH_MAX=8 CONTINUOUS_BATCH_WAIT_MS=20
```

devon-eng: throttle applied, rolling restart initiated for canary pods.

priya-sre: starting compaction job to purge transient excess kv entries and enable a soft cap (kv_cardinality_limit=200k). Running compaction now.

priya-sre: metrics update (4m after mitigations): kv_entries down 1.1M -> ~45k, continuous-batcher queue normalized, p95 gen latency down to ~120ms, 5xx back to baseline.

emily-support: notified acme-co and bizly via their support channels, raised tickets for both. acme-co reported ~12 failed requests during window, all retried successfully; bizly saw increased latencies but no permanent failures.

sam-rl: root-cause hypothesis: the interaction of sliding-window prefetch + NTK expansion increases unique KV prefixes per request. Continuous-batcher merged multiple such requests, producing a large set of unique prefix keys (no dedupe), blowing out KV memory/cardinality.

matt-runtime: pushing hotpatch to add per-request prefix dedupe + hard cap on number of prefixes we prefetch. PR: https://github.com/redwood/rope-runtime/pull/4987 (hotfix e3f9c1a) — will cap at 64 unique prefixes per request and dedupe across batch.

jordan-oncall: good. immediate mitigations worked. moving to monitoring mode. follow-ups:
- add alert: kv_cardinality > 100k (page SRE)
- add canary safety: block sliding-window if ENABLE_YARN && PREFETCH_WINDOW > 1024 unless canary traffic < 1%
- add batching dedupe + limits in runtime (matt's PR)
- runbook update for similar incidents (NTK/YaRN-related cache growth)
- customer comms postmortem draft (emily to lead)

leah-oncall: I'm next on-call for morning shift, taking handoff. I'll pick up the follow-ups and schedule a postmortem. Please add any logs/links to the incident doc.

jordan-oncall: tagging the incident RESOLVED for now (metrics stable > 15m). Handing off to leah-oncall for RCA and customer follow-through.

incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — kv_cardinality below threshold for 20m. Auto-clear in 15m if no regressions.

leah-oncall: got it, I'll own the postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks everyone for the quick response. :thumbsup:
